# zungrq

> Generates an M-by-N complex matrix Q with orthonormal rows, defined as the last M rows of a product of K elementary reflectors of order N.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zungrq from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zungrq';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zungrq( order, M, N, K, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows of Q (M >= 0) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `N < M` | number of columns of Q (N >= M) |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > M` | number of elementary reflectors (0 <= K <= M) |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, M )`; row-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `K` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | in |  |  | `TAU` stride length |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, M )` |  | workspace of length at least `max(1,M)`; `M*NB` (`NB = 32`) enables the blocked path when `K > 128`; if `null`, a workspace of the optimal size is allocated |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q. $N \ge M$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. $M \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the (m-k+i)-th row must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by ZGERQF in the last k rows of its array argument A. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by ZGERQF.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `N < M`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > M`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zungrq.ndarray(
    M, N, K,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows of Q (M >= 0) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `N < M` | number of columns of Q (N >= M) |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > M` | number of elementary reflectors (0 <= K <= M) |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input/output matrix (M x N) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A (complex elements) |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `K` |  | scalar factors of reflectors (length K) |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for TAU (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for TAU (complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, M )` |  | workspace of length at least `max(1,M)`; `M*NB` (`NB = 32`) enables the blocked path when `K > 128` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK (complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q. $N \ge M$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. $M \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the (m-k+i)-th row must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by ZGERQF in the last k rows of its array argument A. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by ZGERQF.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `N < M`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > M`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `M <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument has an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zungrq()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZUNGRQ`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zungrq.f).
-   `Q` is defined as `Q = H(1)^H H(2)^H ... H(K)^H`, where each `H(i)` is an elementary reflector.
-   The blocked algorithm uses `NB = 32` and falls back to `ZUNGR2` for the leading unblocked block.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zungrq from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zungrq';

const M = 3;
const N = 4;
const K = M;
const A = new Complex128Array( M * N );
const TAU = new Complex128Array( K );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( M * 32 );

// Using the standard interface (column-major):
let out = zungrq( 'column-major', M, N, K, A, M, TAU, 1, WORK );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zungrq.ndarray( M, N, K, A, 1, M, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZUNGRQ`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZUNGRQ generates an M-by-N complex matrix Q with orthonormal rows, which is defined as the last M rows of a product of K elementary reflectors of order N

$$
Q = H(1)^H H(2)^H \cdots H(k)^H
$$

as returned by ZGERQF.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
